title: Canonical monoidal derived pullback of pro-etale internal modules
statement: Let Λ be a commutative condensed ring, X and Y schemes, and f : X → Y. The left derived pullback L(f*Λ) on unbounded derived categories of internal module objects is strong monoidal. Its comonoidal tensor map is the universal left-derived tensor comparison, and its unit map is the derived counit on the unit followed by the ordinary unit comparison in degree zero. Both tensor counits are natural transformations, and the comparison between their two derived bifunctors is invertible.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9(3), Proposition 6.8.11(3); canonical derived tensor construction as formalized by new-integral-residue-derived-monoidal

proof.text: Construct the homotopy tensor counit as the lax tensorator of Qh followed by Qh of the inverse natural comonoidal comparison for the exact monoidal pullback. Tensor the derived pullback counit in both arguments and compose with this homotopy counit. The opposite derived counit is the existing leftDerivedDerivedTensorCounit. Composition and whiskering prove all four naturality laws.

Identify pullback with mapModComap along the inverse of the coefficient comparison. Transport flatness along extendScalarsIsoComapInv and apply inverseImageModule_preservesFlat. The generic canonical comparison is derived using flat preservation. For the original concrete right counit, retain the existing upstream two-variable derived universal-property instance and transport it through the explicit counit equality from step 3.

Use the proved generic residueDerivedMonoidal construction. Its canonical tensor comparison and counit satisfy the lax square, its coherence descends along kFlatMap resolutions, and its tensor and unit maps are invertible. The unit of Qh is the identity. Expand the homotopy functor unit comparison and its single-complex comparison to identify the descended unit map with leftDerivedTensorUnitIso. Copy the monoidal structure using these equal explicit unit maps. Specialize this constructed structure to the exact monoidal pullback using the flatness result of the preceding step. For the generic lift, postcompose the canonical comparison's component formula with the inverse homotopy comonoidal comparison. Cancel the inverse pair and apply the derived bifunctor universal property. This proves homotopyTensorLeftDerivedLift_eq without the former general-purpose transport chain. After the upstream sync, identify the retained degreewise tensor map with mapCochainComplexμIso.hom using its summand formula. Cancel the homotopy comonoidal isomorphism to identify the homotopy counits; then identify both derived counits componentwise. Apply the two-variable derived uniqueness theorem with these equal counits to identify the original upstream lift with the generic canonical comparison. The upstream monoidal instance is retained in its source module without edits.
